why.rationale: The operator enters one vestibule — argv parse, mode detection, run_id, RUN_DIR setup — then hits a single decision-point at line 184: read .pattern. Two doors open from there. Door A (parallel) is a straight hallway: walk chain[] once, one envelope per stage, exit. Door B (pair-relay) is a turnstile chamber: walk sequence[] N times, c1.00 / c1.01 / c2.00 envelope-naming carves cycle-rings into the floor. The decision is invisible at the front desk — the operator can't tell which door they'll be sent through until the YAML is parsed. Both doors share the vestibule but diverge into mutually-exclusive corridors guarded by `if PAIR_RELAY_FLOW == 0 ... fi` wrapping 215 lines of the older hallway.
decisions_considered: switch-yard (rejected — implies parallel tracks; this is sequential gate)
fork-in-the-road (rejected — too neutral; doesn't name the asymmetry)
elevator-with-two-floors (rejected — implies same shape at both destinations)
branch-room-with-shared-foyer (close, but understates the data-shape asymmetry)
tools_used: route-language translation (each if/for reframed as door/hallway/turnstile)
default-tracing (which door does an unmarked ticket lead to?)
